cohort: 75 infants born vaginally or by planned versus emergent C-section
finding: While infants born by C-section can initially have Bacteroides in their gut, they lack this bacteria by 2 weeks of age, suggesting that colonization stability, rather than birth canal exposure, is more important for gut microbiome composition.
mod_finding: Infants born by C-section, whether planned or emergent (and therefore exposed or not exposed to the vaginal canal), lack Bacteroides species in their gut by 2 weeks of age.
